questions.prompt: What's the difference between a lightweight and an annotated tag?

options.text: Lightweight tags move with the branch; annotated tags don't
A lightweight tag is just a name pointing at a commit; an annotated tag is a full object storing tagger, date, and message
Annotated tags can only be used on GitHub

questions.explanation: A lightweight tag is a bare pointer; an annotated tag is a full object with tagger, date, and message (and can be signed), which is why it's preferred for releases.

questions.prompt: In SemVer MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH, which part increments for a backward-compatible bug fix?

options.text: None — bug fixes don't change the version

questions.explanation: A backward-compatible bug fix bumps PATCH (e.g. 1.4.2 → 1.4.3). MINOR is for backward-compatible features; MAJOR is for breaking changes.

questions.prompt: Which statements are true? Select all that apply.

options.text: Tags are not pushed by default; you push them explicitly
A GitHub Release is built on top of a Git tag
Annotated tags store a message and tagger
A MAJOR bump is for backward-compatible additions

questions.explanation: Tags need an explicit push, Releases anchor to tags, and annotated tags carry metadata. Backward-compatible additions bump MINOR, not MAJOR.

questions.prompt: In semantic versioning, a change that breaks backward compatibility increments the ______ number.
questions.explanation: Breaking, incompatible changes bump the MAJOR version (e.g. 1.4.2 → 2.0.0).

questions.prompt: A project is at 1.4.2. You add a new feature that doesn't break existing usage. What should the next version be?
questions.explanation: A new backward-compatible feature bumps MINOR and resets PATCH to 0: 1.4.2 → 1.5.0.

questions.prompt: Match each item to its description.

pairs.right: A plain pointer to a commit
Full object with tagger and message
A tag plus notes and assets

questions.explanation: Lightweight is a bare pointer, annotated carries metadata, a Release adds notes/assets to a tag, and MAJOR marks breaking changes.
